In `app/bg_jobs.py`, I removed the `MAX_TIMER_TIMEOUT` constant. In `BgJobManager.create`, `timeout_seconds` is now clamped to `[1, MAX_TIMEOUT]` for every job type. For timers, the result is then raised to at least `delay_seconds + 3600`, with no upper cap. A 10-day timer now gets `expires_at` an hour after `trigger_at`, and other job types behave as before. I haven't run any tests.

One edge case: a timer whose delay plus 3600 exceeds `MAX_TIMEOUT` can have a lifetime above `MAX_TIMEOUT`. I did this deliberately, because the "at least delay + 3600 for any delay" requirement takes priority over the clamp.
